'''Manfred Baerns''' (23 July 1934 – 2 February 2021) was a German chemist.

==Career==
After a 2-years postdoctoral fellowship at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]] (Argonne, Illinois), a further 5 years in academia and a 5-year career in industry, was a full professor for chemical technology and reaction engineering at [[Ruhr University|Ruhr-University Bochum]] (Germany) from 1974&ndash;1995. He then acted as scientific director of the "Institute of Applied Chemistry Berlin-Adlershof" until 2003.<ref>http://www.adlershof.de/fileadmin/downloads/pub/AM/Adlershof-Magazin5.pdf; Adlershof Magazin (no. 5, 2002, p. 31-34)</ref>{{full citation needed|date=September 2026}} He was lately a guest scientist as [[Professor|Professor Emeritus]] at the "Fritz-Haber-Institute" of the Max-Planck-Society at Berlin.{{Cn|date=September 2026}}

Baerns was a member of numerous scientific committees and a referee for research proposal at a national level. From 1991 to 1997 he was member of the board DECHEMA (a scientific association of chemical technology, [[chemical engineering]] and biotechnology), and a permanent member of the German [[Chemical Society]], the German Bunsen Society for [[Physical chemistry|Physical Chemistry]], German Society for Coal, Oil and Gas, and finally the [[American Chemical Society]].{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}}

He received the DECHEMA titanium medal,<ref>http://www.dechema.de/Wir+über+uns-p-216/Preisträger+DECHEMA_Plakette-p-1052.html {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref> the award of the [[4th World]] Congress on Oxidation Catalysis, for which he acted as president, honorary professorships of the Humboldt University and the [[University of Technology|Technical University]], both at Berlin, honorary membership of the Leibniz-Institute for Catalysis at Rostock (Germany).{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}}

Baerns was an author of about 300 scientific publications<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?as_q=&num=10&btnG=Search+Scholar&as_epq=&as_oq=&as_eq=&as_occt=any&as_sauthors=Manfred+Baerns&as_publication=&as_ylo=&as_yhi=&as_allsubj=all&hl=en&lr= Google Scholar]</ref>{{full citation needed|date=September 2026}} and three books on [[chemical reaction]] engineering and catalysis. His research focused on [[heterogeneous catalysis]] (oil and gas for chemicals) and chemical reaction engineering.

He died in February 2021 at the age of 86.<ref>[https://trauer.tagesspiegel.de/traueranzeige/manfred-baerns Manfred Baerns] {{in lang|de}}</ref>
